title: Weight-space programming for tractor guidance controller: large language models natively write neural network weights that steer a real tractor
read_level: full (PDF via pdftotext; main text, tables 4-6, limitations; appendix prompt skimmed)
why_wsp: GPT-6 Astra and Claude Fable 5.1 (no tools, text only) read a 253-weight steering network as JSON and write new weight values, both repairing a PPO-trained network for a slower actuator and writing a controller into all-zero weights, using up to 25 simulated evaluations as feedback.
domain: agricultural robotics: tractor path-tracking (closed-loop steering control), sim and real field test
editor: GPT-6 Astra (gpt-6-astra, reasoning effort high); Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1, effort high); quick check with Claude Fable 5.2
target: 253-parameter steering network (token encoder 9-4-4, 60 params; head 22-8-1, 193 params)
interface: direct values (weights as JSON text; no code execution)
loop: closed-loop with feedback (25 simulated evaluations on 64 feedback paths); also a one-shot zero-shot repair test (10 Fable agents)
self_editing: no; LLMs write a separate small controller network
fraction_or_count_of_weights_changed: Astra repair: "144 of 253 weights changing and 32 being set to zero"; Fable repair: "227 trained weights were set to zero and none of the others kept its value, leaving 25 non-zero weights" (Sec 4.5); from zero: "53 and 50 non-zero weights of 253" (Sec 4.6)

headline_results.claim: Repair of S1 with feedback (held-out J, failures/512)
headline_results.where: Table 5 (budget, J, failures, max, non-zero); S1 start J 190.53, 352 failures

headline_results.quote: Two of the ten proposals repaired the network, which resulted in no failures on the unseen paths and a lower error than the start

headline_results.claim: Writing from zero weights; ES fails
headline_results.quote: Both LLMs wrote a working steering controller into the all-zero network, where no failures occurred on the unseen paths ... the evolution strategy with 1000 evaluations also failed every path
headline_results.where: Sec 4.6; Table 5 (AS-0 J 4.94, FA-0 J 7.00; pure pursuit J 6.98)

headline_results.quote: PPO on the same 253 parameters from scratch (GD-T) and fine-tuned from S1 (GD-1) both had a lower error than every LLM controller
headline_results.where: Sec 4.7; Table 5 (GD-T J 3.43, GD-1 J 2.78, 20M steps)

headline_results.quote: GPT-6 Astra identified 248 of 248 correctly, whereas Claude Fable 5.1 identified 227 of 248
Both models identified 89 of 96 signs of the input effects per hidden unit correctly
the gains implied by these numbers matched the measured gains within 3 % in the design from zero, such as the inner-loop gain of turn 1, −11.46 stated versus −11.459 measured
The RMS lateral error ranged from 12.6 cm (GD-1) to 27.8 cm (FA-0) ... The pure pursuit controller achieved 18.5 cm, and the repair by Fable (FA-1) reached 19.8 cm

cost.where: Table 4 (S1 Astra, S1 Fable, S0 Astra, S0 Fable); API time total 934 / 2512 / 1676 / 4157 s

cost.quote: training with proximal policy optimisation requires samples, compute and tuning, which needed 20 million simulated steps per network in this study

baselines_and_controls: Gain grid (25 evals); (1+1) evolution strategy over all 253 weights (5 seeds, 25 and 1000 evals, plus noisy-zero starts); pure pursuit (tuned look-ahead); PPO from scratch (GD-T), PPO fine-tuned from S1 (GD-1), PPO from LLM design (AS-0-GD), PPO from noisy zero (98 seeds per noise level).
runs_and_variance: "one session per model and start point without performing statistical tests" (Sec 6.8); zero-shot test 10 repetitions; ES 5 seeds; PPO-from-zero 98 seeds with min-max reported.
robustness_of_edits: Sim-to-real transfer tested: all four LLM controllers steered the real tractor without intervention; PPO started from LLM designs converged (AS-0-GD). No quantization/distribution-shift tests beyond field.
verification: Exact linearised discrete closed-loop analysis (stability, damping) of every controller; LLM-stated control laws checked against measured gains; held-out 512 paths. No formal proof.
memorization_vs_reasoning: LLM designs are sparse cascaded classical controllers; stated gains match measured gains (Fable within 3%); reasoning summaries show model-based design then one-parameter tuning. Paper cautions summaries are provider-written: "they show what was documented rather than how the model computed" (Sec 6.1).
limitations_stated: One session per model and start point, no statistical tests; repair sessions doubled as prompt development; single tractor, speed, path, field; one 253-param network and 25-eval budget; only pure pursuit as classical baseline; depends on vendors keeping closed models available.
cites_or_builds_on: Takehi et al., Sparks of Weight-Space Programming (blog, 2026-11-02)
Zhang et al. (2026), robot policy embedding edit
Salloum and Ali (2026), non-LLM method from agent logs
notes_for_survey: First WSP study with a continuous physical plant and a real-machine test; LLMs write from zero where equal-budget ES and gradient descent (exact zero) cannot start. Coins 'Weight-Space Engineering' for WSP embedded in an engineering process with explicit cost and verification. Astra edited the trained net while Fable 5.1 replaced it; Fable 5.2 edited like Astra.
